issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor drops the outer Delimited, silently narrowing multi-action ALTER support.
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped actions in Delimited(OneOf(...)), allowing comma-separated heterogeneous actions like ADD col, DROP COLUMN in a single ALTER TABLE. The new grammar is OneOf only, removing this capability without justification. The deleted fixture exercised exactly this MSDN-documented form. Either restore the outer Delimited or document the scope reduction explicitly.

issues.description: Removed valid mixed ADD/DROP ALTER TABLE fixture without replacement coverage or justification.
issues.detail: The deleted statement combining ADD column with CONSTRAINT and DROP COLUMN variants is documented T-SQL syntax. The commit claims it was invalid without citation, and no replacement coverage was added. This combines with the grammar narrowing to silently remove a supported feature.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT folded under shared DROP head erodes named-subtype dispatch.
issues.detail: Folding both DROP variants under a single outer DROP keyword with inner Delimited forces downstream rules, formatters, and fixers to disambiguate by lookahead at the next keyword rather than dispatching on a named alter_table_action subtype. Consider distinct subtypes for column versus constraint drops to preserve the structural contract.

issues.description: Four unrelated grammar changes shipped as a single bundled patch.
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN identifiers, negative IDENTITY seed, and ALTER TABLE DROP refactor are independent features touching different segments. Bundling them prevents independent revert, bisect, or refusal on individual merits. These should land as four separate patches.

issues.description: IDENTITY grammar permissively accepts SignedSegment on increment without test or comment.
issues.detail: IDENTITY(seed, increment) allows a leading sign on both positions, admitting values the engine rejects. No fixture exercises a negative increment. Either add a fixture for IDENTITY(-1,-1), constrain the grammar to the seed only, or add a short comment stating the parser is intentionally permissive with semantic validation deferred.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no fixture or rationale comment.
issues.detail: The grammar gains a NumericLiteralSegment alternative for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE (presumably the LCID form), but the new fixture only exercises the identifier path. Either add a fixture covering the numeric LCID, drop the alternative, or add a one-line comment documenting the LCID intent so the contract is legible.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a competent T-SQL grammar extension undermined by a bundling problem and a silent contract narrowing in ALTER TABLE. The outer Delimited was dropped from ALTER TABLE actions, removing multi-action support, and a fixture exercising that form was deleted without justification. The DROP refactor also folds COLUMN and CONSTRAINT under a shared head, weakening named-subtype dispatch for downstream tools. Smaller issues: IDENTITY increment and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric forms are added permissively with no test coverage or documenting comment. Recommend splitting the patch, restoring or justifying the ALTER TABLE scope change, and adding fixtures for the new grammar alternatives.
